newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian financier goes to prison in graft scandal.
newsitem.headline: Italian financier goes to prison in graft scandal.

text.p: Italian financier Sergio Cusani, who helped expose rampant corruption at the heart of Italy's political old guard, turned himself in to prison authorities on Wednesday to begin a four year sentence for bribery.
Cusani, the first major personality to be convicted in Italy's "Tangentopoli" (Bribesville) scandals, arrived at Milan's notorious San Vittore prison with suitcase in hand.

"I am at peace with myself. I will try to build something useful for people inside prison, where life carries on even if it's not a very good life," Cusani told reporters before entering the imposing jail.

Cusani was convicted two years ago for his part in a scandal over bribes paid by insurance firm SAI to win contracts from energy group ENI. He was the main figure in another major graft trial centred on ENI which is currently under appeal.
Italy's highest court confirmed Cusani's jail term on Tuesday and also upheld sentences on former Italian prime minister Bettino Craxi and nine others.
Milan magistrates on Wednesday asked the Justice Ministry to issue an international arrest warrant for Craxi on the basis of the latest court decision, judicial sources said.
It would be the second arrest warrant issued against Craxi, who lives in self-imposed exile in Tunisia and has said he will not return to Italy just to go to jail.
Craxi faces a jail term of five and half years for the SAI saga and has more than 25 years of prison sentences accumulated against him from other trials.

The high court also confirmed sentences against former SAI president Salvatore Ligresti and managing director Fausto Rapisardo, former Christian Democrat party treasurer Severino Citaristi and two former ENI executives.
It also upheld a four-year conviction of Marcello Di Giovanni, the former head of insurer Padana Assicurazioni, who was arrested in Rome on Wednesday, police said.
They said they were still looking for former ENI executives Antonio Sernia and Alberto Grotti, whose arrest was requested earlier on Wednesday by the Milan prosecutor's office.
The Tangentopoli scandals broke in February 1992 when the manager of a Milan old people's home confessed to taking bribes on behalf of Craxi's Socialist party.
His confession led to other confessions and prosecutors soon cracked open an entrenched system of bribes-for-public contracts involving politicians and businessmen.
Few were spared in the judicial assault. Before Cusani only one other person, an obscure Milan councillor, has actually served a prison term arising from the scandals.
San Vittore prison became a symbol of the scandals in 1993 after former ENI chairman Gabriele Cagliari killed himself in a cell there while under investigation for graft.
